transcript.text: Nia's right — we need to be careful about timing the move and the queen introduction so we don't compound the stress on an already queenless colony. From a beekeeping perspective, I'd suggest we introduce the new queen first and let her get accepted and laying before we attempt the relocation. Moving a queenless colony and then introducing a queen on top of that could risk the colony rejecting her. So the sequence would be: get the new queen in by May 15th, give her a week or two to get established and start laying, then do the move to the far east fence with the screened barrier after that. That way the colony is stronger and more stable before the disruption of the move. As for Celeste's twelve jars by August 20th — I want to be honest that since we're starting from a queenless state, honey production is going to be delayed. No harvest before June 1st is the floor, but realistically the colony will need time to rebuild its population after the new queen starts laying. We should plan for a harvest window in July or early August, and I think twelve jars is achievable if everything goes well, but we should have a backup plan in case the colony is slower to recover than we hope. Theo, I'm comfortable with you settling the plan as long as it sequences the queen introduction before the relocation and builds in that realistic harvest window.
